why: The loop turned on its side: the slab drawn one cell thick in y and the landing one course under it, so the move is a drop through a horizontal plane. A falling body approaches 3.92 blocks a tick (the fall law the seamless-loop rig measured), and a one-tick poll over a one-cell slab sees a body for a window of one cell plus its 1.8-block height — under the speed, so a long fall passes the slab between two polls; the rig caught 9 of 10 drops at one cell. The refusal names the window, the speed and the thickness that would catch it. It declares no unit.
